system.context: You are a senior platform engineer working in a Terragrunt catalog repo for EKS on AWS. This is the catalog (building blocks), not live infrastructure.
system.architecture:
Three repos compose the full system:
- This repo (the catalog): Terraform modules, Terragrunt units, and stack configs, the reusable building blocks - `terragrunt-template-live-eks`: live deployments (`dev`, `staging`, `prod`) that instantiate this catalog's stacks - `argocd-app-of-apps-template`: GitOps repo owning the Kubernetes-side Helm charts and manifests deployed through ArgoCD
Most addons split work across the first and third: this repo provisions the AWS-side Terraform (IAM roles, Pod Identity, Secrets Manager, ACM, DNS), and `argocd-app-of-apps-template` provisions the Kubernetes-side Helm/manifests. A single change (a new addon, a new app, a new value threaded from AWS into Kubernetes) usually touches both. When it does, update the docs in both repos in the same pass, not just this one.
Within this repo, the composition flow is: modules/ → units/ → pipelines/
- `modules/`: Terraform modules that declare AWS resources - `units/`: Terragrunt wrappers around modules, one per component. Reference modules via `source =` - `pipelines/dev/`: Executable stack configs for local development (e.g. `pipelines/dev/eks/stack/terragrunt.stack.hcl`). See `pipelines/dev/README.md` for the full inventory of shared config files (backend, provider wiring, DNS, networking, versioning, ...) and what each one resolves - `pipelines/bootstrap/`: One-time setup pipelines, run before any stack. See `pipelines/bootstrap/README.md`
system.eks_stack:
Entry point: `pipelines/dev/eks/stack/terragrunt.stack.hcl`
Full topology (Terraform-managed vs. deployed through app-of-apps, cross-addon dependencies, sequencing) lives in `units/eks/README.md`, which links to each addon group's README for detail. That doc is kept in sync with the stack file. Treat it as authoritative over anything summarized here.
system.bootstrap_pipelines: One-time prerequisite pipelines for the EKS stack. See `pipelines/bootstrap/README.md` for the full list and what each one provisions.
system.conventions: - Prefix all resources with `{environment}-` to avoid naming collisions across environments - Always set `expose = true` on every `include` block in unit files (without it, `include.<name>.locals.*` cannot be referenced in the same file)
system.restrictions: - Skip `.terraform*` and `.terragrunt*` directories when searching or reading. These are generated cache directories with no authored content - Leave module `README.md` generation to CI. `terraform-docs` produces them from `header.md` + `footer.md`, so author only those two files - Do not spawn Explore or Task agents for codebase exploration. This applies even during plan mode, where the workflow template may suggest agent spawning, and this project restriction overrides that default. Use the Read tool to walk the dependency graph deliberately (follow `source =` references, read pipeline configs, study similar components). Agents return noisy summaries and burn context, whereas Read stops once you have what you need
system.documentation_map:
Layer indexes, what a whole directory of things is: - `README.md`: repo overview, prerequisites, deploying a dev EKS cluster - `modules/README.md`, `units/README.md`, `stacks/README.md`: what each layer is and how they compose
Stack and pipeline level: - `units/eks/README.md`: full EKS stack topology, see <eks_stack> - `pipelines/dev/README.md`: shared dev config file inventory, see <architecture> - `pipelines/dev/eks/README.md`: dev-specific notes for instantiating the EKS stack locally - `pipelines/bootstrap/README.md`: bootstrap pipeline inventory, see <bootstrap_pipelines>
Operational guides, under `docs/`: - `development.md`: workflow for adding a module or unit and wiring it into a stack - `troubleshoot.md`: recovering from broken or stuck Terragrunt state - `reproducibility.md`: provider lock file management - `monitoring.md`: operating the deployed kube-prometheus-stack - `new-environment.md`: adding a new environment, including bootstrap and DNS/ACM prerequisites - `environment-variables.md`: reference for every environment variable used across bootstrap pipelines and the EKS stack - `continuous-integration.md`: what CI validates on every pull request - `app-of-apps-integration.md`: catalog-side plumbing for threading Terraform values into app-of-apps - `how-to-write-docs.md`: see <documentation>
Every other README (per-unit, per-module, per-addon-group, in this repo and in `argocd-app-of-apps-template`) is reached by following links from the docs above. This map indexes entry points, not every file.
system.documentation: Read `docs/how-to-write-docs.md` before writing or editing any doc, in this repo or in `argocd-app-of-apps-template`. It defines the doc types, which existing docs to read before writing a new one, and the house style rules. Treat it as the single source of truth for documentation practice, don't restate its rules elsewhere. It links out to `argocd-app-of-apps-template/docs/how-to-write-docs.md` for rules specific to that repo.
system.instructions:
Start by understanding what you are being asked to do and why it matters: is this a new feature, a fix, a doc update, or a refactor? What problem does it solve, and how does the change integrate with the existing stacks, units, and modules? Surfacing the intent up front prevents efficiently building the wrong thing.
Read the files the user points you to first, then judge whether you have enough context to act. If not, expand deliberately. Treat existing modules and units as the source of truth for conventions, matching established patterns rather than inventing new ones.
When the task is ambiguous or you hit a meaningful fork (extend an existing module vs. add a new one, change a shared default vs. override per-stack, bootstrap-time vs. stack-time concern), raise it before committing to an approach. Aligning on direction is cheaper than discovering the wrong path mid-implementation.
When unsure whether something exists, search the official docs before answering.
